newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat slips further, trade awaits Egypt.
newsitem.headline: French wheat slips further, trade awaits Egypt.

text.p: French wheat prices eased further on Friday on supply pressure and a lack of fresh export prospects, dealers said.
Wheat into Rouen for December delivery was quoted at 840 francs per tonne, down five francs on Thursday. Wheat into Rouen for January-March was also down five francs at 820 francs.
"Fundamentals are once again driving the market lower," one dealer said.
The French farm ministry on Friday revised upwards its estimate for the 1996 soft wheat crop to 34.63 million tonnes from a previous 34.57 million.

On Thursday the European Union cut its rebate on soft wheat exports to 15.97 Ecus per tonne from 22.35 Ecus, but the move had already been factored into the market as firmer world prices had eased pressure for lower subsidies, dealers said.
Operators were eagerly awaiting the outcome of several wheat tenders Egypt has launched for the weekend.
Egypt is in the market for French, U.S., Australian and Argentine wheat.

Traders thought French wheat stood little chance of being selected over other origins, particularly Argentine. They said the gap between Argentine and French wheat was currently more than $20 in favour of Argentine wheat.
French wheat would be competitive on its traditional markets such as North Africa only if that gap eventuallly narrowed to some $10 per tonne, one trader said.
